metric_rationale: The metric zeroes in on two critical trial types where Tallying and WADD have strictly opposite preferences. In Trial 1, Option B has more winning features (3 vs 2) but Option A's features are highly valid (0.95+0.90 > 0.60+0.55+0.50). In Trial 8, Option A has more winning features (2 vs 1) but Option B's single winning feature is the most valid (0.95 > 0.60+0.55). The metric computes the proportion of times the subject chooses the Tallying-preferred option on these critical trials. Tallying will yield a high score, while WADD will yield a low score.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Weighted Additive (WADD) model on 'dissociation' trials. On these specific trials (Trial 1 and Trial 2), one option is superior on the two most valid features (favored by WADD), while the other option is superior on the three least valid features (favored by Tallying). WADD agents will consistently score high on this metric (close to 1), whereas Tallying agents will score low (close to 0), producing a large and stable gap between the two theories.
